transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

Well, I came in because... I just can't shake this certainty that I'm being punished. It's about my father. He's been declining, and I feel like it's my fault, like I let it happen. My sister keeps showing me the doctor's notes and telling me I've done everything right, but... it doesn't matter. It still feels like some kind of judgment has already been passed on me, and I can't get past it.
Over the past few weeks or months, how has your overall mood been? Are you feeling sad or empty most of the time, or is it mainly this guilt and self-blame about your father that's bothering you?

It's not just the guilt about my dad. Um... most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling. It's almost like the color has just gone out of everything. I can sit at my desk at work—I'm in HR—or... or just stare at the garden beds at home, and I just feel like none of it reaches me anymore. So, yes, that sad or empty feeling is definitely there most of the time, on top of everything else.
Have you experienced periods like this before—where you felt this same heavy, hollow sadness and loss of interest in things—at other times in your life?

No, I haven't. I mean, I've had normal ups and downs, like anyone else. Stressful times at work, or when my dad first started getting sick... but nothing like this. I've never felt this kind of constant, heavy emptiness before. It's completely new, and it just won't go away.
How long have you been experiencing this heavy, hollow feeling and loss of interest in things? Can you think back to when it started?

It's been going on for a while now... about a year and two months, I'd say. That's when my father's health really started to change, and his behavior got worse. I had to step in and take over his caregiving around then, and... well, that's when this whole feeling started settling in.

During these past 14 months, have you noticed changes in how you move or act—like feeling slowed down, moving more slowly, or speaking more slowly than usual? Or on the other hand, have you felt restless or agitated, like you can't sit still?

Yes, definitely the slowed down part. I haven't felt restless at all, just... really sluggish. People at work have actually started asking if I'm sick, just because I move so slowly through my normal, routine tasks now. And in meetings... um, sometimes it takes me a noticeable moment just to process and answer even simple questions. It's like my body and my brain are just operating on a delay.

You mentioned feeling like you're being punished and that judgment has been passed on you—when you think about these ideas, do you ever hear voices or see things that others around you don't seem to experience?

Yes... I do. I haven't seen anything, but... at night, when the house gets really quiet, I sometimes hear a woman's voice. It sounds just as clear as if she's standing right out in the hallway. She just says, 'You failed him.' It sounds so real that I've actually gotten up more than once to go check the hall, even though I know there's no one else there.
When you hear that voice saying 'You failed him,' do you believe it's real—like an actual person speaking to you—or do you know it's something your mind is creating, even though it sounds real?

I... I'm really not sure. It's confusing. When I hear it, it sounds so real, like there's actually a woman standing right there in the hall. That's why I get up to check. But then... when I look and no one is there, I know it can't be a real person. But in the moment, it just feels entirely real.

When you hear that voice at night saying 'You failed him,' in that moment while you're hearing it, do you actually believe there is a real woman standing in the hallway speaking to you, or do you know it's not real even as you're hearing it?

I don't really know for sure. In the exact second I hear it, I guess... I do think she's really out there. My heart jumps, and my first instinct is that someone is in the house. But almost immediately, like as I'm getting out of bed to look, logic kicks in and I know it's impossible. So... right in that split second, I don't really know how to explain it. It just sounds completely real, and my body reacts like it's real.

Outside of these moments when you hear the voice, when you're thinking clearly during the day, do you still believe that you actually failed your father and are being punished—or do you recognize that your sister was right when she showed you the doctor's notes proving you did everything you could?

Even during the day, when I'm thinking clearly... I still believe it. I know my sister showed me the doctor's notes, and she tells me I did everything right, but... I just can't shake the certainty that I failed him. It doesn't matter what the paperwork says. It still feels, deep down, like I'm being punished for letting him decline. Like this judgment has already been passed on me, and nothing anyone says can change it.

When you think about the idea that you failed your father and are being punished—if I told you that medical experts reviewed his care and confirmed you did everything appropriately, would that evidence be able to change your mind, or does the feeling of guilt and punishment persist no matter what anyone tells you?

I don't think it would change my mind. Honestly... I came in here because I just can't shake this absolute certainty that I'm being punished for letting him decline. Like I said before, my sister has already shown me the doctor's notes. She tells me I did everything right. But it doesn't matter what the evidence says or what anyone tells me. It just feels like... like this judgment has already been passed on me, and nothing is going to change that.
